H&P – Detailed Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
40-year-old female with 3-week history of left-sided hearing reduction, facial numbness, intermittent tinnitus, and occasional dizziness; clinician suspects Bell’s palsy and arranged same-day face-to-face neurological/otoscopic examination.

History:
• Chief complaints: Reduced hearing in left ear and numbness over left peri-auricular jawline.  
• Onset & course: Gradual over ~3 weeks; persistent; no documented progression trend.  
• Associated symptoms: Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in left ear; occasional dizziness temporally related to tinnitus.  
• Denies: Ear discharge, ear pain, pruritus, fever, dysphagia, dysarthria, limb weakness/numbness, vision changes.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified.  
• Review of systems otherwise non-contributory per transcript.

Past Medical History:
• Nasal polyps – episodic; uses intranasal steroid spray PRN (name not recalled).  
• Remote history of labyrinthitis – resolved.  
• Occasional dyspepsia/heartburn – self-treats with Rennie (OTC antacid).  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Intranasal spray for nasal polyps – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Rennie (calcium/magnesium carbonate antacid) – dose/route/frequency not documented; PRN.  

Allergies:
• Latex – documented allergy.

Social History:
• Occupation: Professional jockey; currently reducing training due to dizziness/tinnitus.  
• Living situation: Lives with partner.  
• Pets: None.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: Not discussed.

Family History:
• Brother diagnosed with neurofibromatosis.  
• No other familial illnesses noted.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed during virtual consult.

Investigations:
• None to date; clinician arranging in-person neurological and otoscopic examination.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Possible Bell’s palsy vs. other unilateral cranial nerve pathology presenting with left facial numbness and hearing reduction.  
  • Arrange same-day face-to-face appointment for full neurological exam, cranial nerve assessment, and otoscopy.  
  • Consider audiometry and imaging (e.g., MRI internal auditory canal) if examination warrants.  
  • Provide preliminary reassurance; advised that condition not thought to be life-threatening.

Issue 2: Symptom-related dizziness/tinnitus.  
  • Evaluate during in-person visit; assess vestibular function.  
  • Manage per findings (e.g., ENT referral if indicated).

Issue 3: Underlying nasal polyps and remote labyrinthitis—currently stable.  
  • Continue intranasal spray PRN.  
  • No change in management at present.

General Plan Items:
• Admin team to schedule urgent clinic visit today; patient instructed to phone support team in 5 minutes to confirm slot.  
• Safety-netting: Attend emergency services if sudden worsening, new neurological deficits, severe headache, or inability to swallow/speak.  
• Documentation of allergy (latex) flagged for clinic.  
• Follow-up: Results of exam and further management to be communicated after evaluation.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing elements: Vitals, physical examination findings, smoking/alcohol history, current medication list reconciliation, name/dose of nasal spray.  
• No internal conflicts noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational overlap but clinically adequate.
